name: Google Gemini
description: Google's multimodal LLM family for reasoning, planning, and structured problem solving
notes: Quality is strong when it actually responds, but the core Gemini model (and CLI) frequently sits in busy/timeout loops which kills flow, so I often favor cheaper-yet-reliable models. Tracking new claims from Addy Osmani about Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite (LinkedIn 2026-03-02: 80% faster than 2.5 Flash, $0.25/M input, $1.50/M output, tunable thinking levels), but need to verify on real projects before trusting it. The YouTube walkthrough at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pJylXFAC87A echoed my own experience: Gemini shines for design tasks yet still struggles with complex coding beyond mockups.

name: OpenCode
description: An open-source, terminal-first AI coding agent that executes tasks directly in your local repo with structured planning and tool use.

name: OpenAI Codex

notes: Same GPT-5.1 Codex limitation as above: screenshot attachments are ignored entirely, so include plaintext context or switch providers. Currently accessed inside OpenCode 1.2.15 via ChatGPT Plus where it provides steady throughput whenever Claude's lower tier is saturated.

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's official terminal-based interface for interacting with Gemini models, focused on coding workflows, structured planning, and local developer integration.
notes: Switch to Gemini CLI when Claude Code hits usage limits. Hasn't completed porting Claude Code plugins to Gemini extension format. Commands are *.toml, skills map 1-1, hooks are different, MCP is similar. When it works it's solid, but lately it just sits "busy" or times out, so I keep cheaper-but-reliable models ready as the default.

name: Claude Code
description: A terminal-based AI coding agent by Anthropic that understands your codebase and executes development tasks via natural language.
notes: Favorite tool in the category. Would use exclusively if not so expensive. $20 tier times out too often on heavy days, and the $100 tier only makes sense when billing high-rate client work, so I'm pairing the cheaper plan with Codex/Minimax instead of paying $100 every month.

name: Goose
description: A local, open-source AI coding agent that autonomously executes engineering tasks like debugging, refactoring, and deployment using your preferred LLM and external MCP servers.
replacementReason: Unstable interface (crashes with OpenAI). When using Gemini, it lacks custom slash commands and feels like a downgraded Gemini CLI.
notes: Tried it and didn't like the interface.

name: Lemon
description: Voice-driven Mac AI agent that turns dictation into tasks (email replies, docs, search, edits) from a single hotkey.
notes: Voice-activated agent that lives in the MacBook notch/menu bar. Two keybindings: one for agent mode (do tasks like writing emails or acting in a browser) and one for dictation mode. Loved the two-for-one (dictation feels free vs Wispr Flow word caps), but it is too buggy: clipboard mode sometimes copies nothing, settings fields randomly disappear, email address is locked, "Check updates" is inert, integrations show as disconnected, and after a few launches the menu stops opening until force quit. Support (support@heylemon.ai) has been responsive per the Attio CRM thread, but I removed it from my stack for reliability.

name: Attio
description: Collaborative CRM used to organize contacts, vendor threads, subscriptions, and refunds with company-level timelines.
notes: Using it beyond sales: every tool/subscription (like Lemon) lives here so I can see the entire support email history at the company level, reply from any thread, and create follow-up tasks for refunds or chargebacks. It doubles as a personal subscription tracker and business CRM in one place.

name: HyperWhisper
description: AI voice-to-text tool that transcribes natural speech in real time to accelerate writing, note-taking, and content creation.
notes: Pricing: Free ($0) includes 3 minutes/day transcription. Pro is $39 lifetime with unlimited transcription; includes lifetime updates, custom vocabulary, priority support, and $5 HyperWhisper Cloud credits. Similar to Wispr Flow and SuperWhisper but positions on simplicity and cloud accuracy vs OS-level voice control or local/offline models.

name: LiteLLM
description: Unified proxy and SDK that standardizes access to multiple LLM providers with a single API and routing, logging, and cost-control features.
notes: OpenAI-compatible API proxy for multi-provider routing, logging, fallback, and cost controls (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, etc.). LangChain is app orchestration; LiteLLM is inference routing/standardization. OpenRouter is hosted routing; LiteLLM is self-hosted proxy control.

name: LLMFit
description: CLI tool for benchmarking, evaluating, and comparing LLM performance across prompts, datasets, and providers to identify the best model for a task.
notes: Lightweight CLI benchmarking for comparing models across providers and prompt sets; simpler than heavier experiment-tracking platforms. Competitive: LangSmith (heavier), Promptfoo (strong prompt testing), OpenAI Evals (OpenAI-focused).

name: Superwhisper
description: AI-powered voice dictation tool that converts speech into structured, formatted text for coding, writing, and agent-driven workflows.
notes: Voice-first dictation aimed at structured/formatted text for coding and writing; emerged alongside agentic coding workflows (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code). Competitive: Wispr Flow (more consumer dictation), MacWhisper (strong local transcription, weaker real-time workflow integration).

name: llama.cpp
description: Open-source C/C++ runtime for efficient local LLM inference across CPUs, GPUs, and edge devices, built for developers shipping offline or self-hosted AI.
notes: Foundational local/embedded inference substrate; differentiates via portability, quantization support, hybrid CPU/GPU execution, and broad hardware coverage. Competitive: Ollama (UX/packaging), vLLM (high-throughput server inference), MLX (Apple-optimized).

name: Wispr Flow
description: AI-powered voice-to-text tool that enables fast, natural dictation for writing, coding, and messaging across applications.
notes: Strong cross-app dictation for writing/coding/messaging. Pain point: limited weekly words; after the quota it becomes noticeably constrained. Competitive: Superwhisper (more agentic/structured), Apple Dictation (less accurate/context-aware for technical long-form).

name: MacWhisper
description: A macOS app that transcribes audio files locally using Whisper and Parakeet for fast, private, high-accuracy speech-to-text.
notes: Local-first transcription (Whisper/Parakeet) optimized for privacy and speed on macOS. Competitive: Otter.ai (collab/cloud), Descript (heavier editing suite), Whisper CLI tools (flexible but less accessible).

name: agent-qa
description: An AI QA agent from vostride for web and mobile testing with persistent memidex memory, validated self-improvement, MCP, and reviewable run evidence.
